data.title: L&T Eyes 20% Share of $150-b Global Modularisation Market
data.description:
Our Bureau Mumbai: Larsen & Toubro (L&T) expects to achieve a 20% or up to $30 billion share of the $150 billion global modularisation market in the next five years, said executives at the engineering and construction conglomerate. "Modularisation is a game changer in the delivery of large and complex energy projects," said Subramanian Sarma, deputy managing director and president, L&T.

He said shifting substantial construction, integration, testing and pre-commissioning activities from a project site to a controlled fabrication environment allows parallel execution, strengthens safety and quality oversight, improves predictability and reduces complexity at site. This will allow L&T to also tide over its labour shortage issue, said Sarma.

S N Subrahmanyan, chairman and managing director, L&T, said the company is currently facing a shortage of 60,000 labourers. Modularisation refers to a project delivery method where entire process units are prefabricated in controlled off-site factories and then transported for rapid on-site assembly. The company Friday announced it has completed fabrication and delivery of 110 modules weighing about 64,000 metric tonnes for Project CERES, Australia's largest urea manufacturing plant with a capacity of 2.3 MTPA.

The project is being developed by Perdaman Chemicals & Fertilisers in Karratha, Western Australia, under the Saipem-Clough joint venture. L&T's pre-assembled 47 units and 63 pre-assembled racks, fabricated at the company's modular fabrication facility at Kattupalli, near Chennai.

The modules were shipped from India to Karratha across 23 marine shipments in fully tested, pre-commissioned and ready-to-install condition, the company said. "We continue to explore new modularisation ideas and data centres, prefabricated bridges, precast columns and other industrial constructed solutions," said Subrahmanyan, adding that the company has also started a cell for doing small modules. "We believe we can do it even further and take on even more complex projects," he said.

data.title: MCX Glitch Leaves Traders Unable to View Positions
data.description:
Our Bureau Mumbai: A delay in the delivery of some end-of-day trade files from the clearing corporation of the Multi Commodity Exchange of India (MCX) left some traders unable to view their positions and average prices on certain broking platforms on Friday, according to people familiar with the matter.

This prompted traders to take to social media, complaining that they were unable to view or square off positions in commodities traded on the exchange. Responding to ET's queries, MCX said, "There was a delay in sending the daily trade file for Sept 17, 2026 to some members from the clearing corporation (CCL). These files have since been sent." The exchange added that all its operations functioned normally on Friday, while trading and settlement activities for Thursday were also normal. Some brokers did not receive the files until late Friday morning, the people said, requesting anonymity. The files contain trade data from the previous trading session and are made available to members before the start of the next session.

data.title: Tata Stocks Reel from Aftershocks as Trusts Opposes 3rd Term for Chandra
data.description:
Our Bureau Mumbai: Tata Group stocks plunged Friday, with Tata Chemicals heading the list of decliners, after Tata Trusts opposed the decision of the Tata Sons board to reappoint N Chandrasekaran as chairman and called the move illegal.

Tata Chemicals fell 11.5% to hit a low of Rs 689.40 on the National Stock Exchange (NSE), while Tata Consultancy Services, India's largest technology outsourcing company, declined nearly 4% to Rs 2,104.90.

Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles fell 3.4%. Tata Investment Corp. retreated 2.5% to Rs 700.95, while Tata Technologies fell 5.24% and Tata Elxsi slipped 1.5%.

These stocks had surged earlier this week on expectations that the central bank's rejection of a Tata Sons application to surrender its licence as a shadow lender would prompt the listing of Tata Sons, the holding company of India's most diversified conglomerate.

Seven listed group companies together hold around 11.94% of Tata Sons. Tata Steel holds 3.06% and Tata Chemicals holds 2.53%, said Gaurav Garg, head-research, Lemonn. "The difference isn't exposure to Tata Sons; it's that Tata Steel's stake is small change against a Rs 2.3 lakh crore business, while Tata Chemicals carries a comparable stake on roughly a fourteenth of the market capitalisation," Garg said. "In the small-cap proxies, the listing narrative is a large share of the price.

That cuts both ways, and today (Friday) it cut one way." On Thursday, the Tata Sons board approved a fresh five-year term for Chandrasekaran and decided to start the process for the holding company's long-awaited initial public offering (IPO). Noel Tata, the chairman of Tata Trusts that majority-owns Tata Sons with a 66% stake, opposed the reappointment of Chandrasekaran, calling it a "legal nullity." Analysts said Friday's selling in Tata stocks reflected investor concerns over the unresolved leadership dispute.

The recent correction in Tata Group stocks needs to be viewed from two key perspectives, said Sunny Agrawal, deputy vice president-Fundamental Research, SBI Securities. Continuity Premium "Any clarity on N Chandrasekaran's continuation as chairman would be sentimentally positive, as it would provide continuity to the group's growth strategy and capital allocation plans and the potential listing of Tata Sons remains an important value-unlocking trigger, particularly for companies that hold a stake in Tata Sons," Agrawal said.

He also said that Tata Chemicals and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles could see meaningful value unlocking if Tata Sons is listed at the expected valuation of around Rs 10 lakh crore.

Tata Chemicals' stake could translate into a value of nearly Rs 30,000 crore, which is significantly higher than its current market capitalisation, while the corresponding value for Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles would be meaningful relative to its market cap.

However, over the longer term, individual businesses are likely to be driven predominantly by their own fundamentals. Within the Tata Group, Tata Consumer, Titan and Indian Hotels are positioned for healthy growth, while Tata Motors Commercial Vehicles appears relatively better placed within the auto segment, analysts said.

Nelco is another company worth tracking, given its exposure to the emerging satellite communication opportunity, they said. Analysts believe that the outcome of Thursday's board meeting has little impact on the operating numbers of Tata Steel, Tata Power or Tata Consumer. "The key issue now is whether the matter moves to a tribunal or is resolved between the board and the Trusts. A negotiated settlement could narrow the discount, while litigation could prolong the uncertainty - with the impact likely to be reflected in the group's listed companies," Lemonn's research head Garg said.

data.title: PIL Challenging Credibility of EVMs used in Assam Election in Gauhati HC
data.description:
Bikash singh Guwahati: A Public Interest Litigation (PIL) has been filed before the Gauhati High Court challenging the credibility and legal acceptability of Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) used in the 2026 Assam Assembly election, with the petitioners raising questions over the semiconductor technology allegedly used in the machines, the disclosure of microchip source code and the reported connection of Japanese semiconductor company Renesas Electronics with Assam's semiconductor initiatives.

The PIL has been filed by Congress leaders Guptamani Sharma and Ripun Bora along with Assam Jatiya Parishad (AJP) leader Ziaur Rahman. The petitioners have alleged that widespread irregularities involving EVMs contributed to the BJP securing a single-party majority in the 2026 Assam Assembly election. These allegations are now before the court for judicial examination.

The maintainability of the PIL came up for hearing before the Chief Justice's court on September 18. According to the petitioners, the court observed that the matter was serious and sensitive and involved issues connected with cases concerning EVMs pending or decided before the Supreme Court and other High Courts. The court indicated that the issues would require detailed consideration and fixed November 4 for the next hearing on maintainability.

The petitioners have pointed out that earlier challenges concerning the reliability of EVMs before the Supreme Court and other High Courts have not resulted in findings establishing that EVMs are inherently unreliable. However, according to the petitioners, the present PIL raises a distinct issue by specifically questioning the microchips or semiconductors used inside the EVMs and the transparency surrounding their programming.

Ziaur Rahman has alleged that the microchips or semiconductor components used in the EVMs were manufactured by the Japan-based company. He has also questioned the extent to which information relating to the programming of such chips is available for public scrutiny. According to Rahman, countries that use electronic voting systems have, in various instances, provided greater disclosure regarding the programming and source code of the relevant technology before elections.

He alleged that the Election Commission of India (ECI) has not made the source code of the relevant EVM technology publicly available. He further referred to an RTI response which, according to him, described the source code as classified information connected with national security. The petitioners have also drawn attention to Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma's reported visit to Japan in January 2025.

Rahman has pointed out that Sarma met representatives of the Japanese company in Tokyo on January 22, 2025. The petitioners have also raised questions over information concerning Assam government efforts to attract semiconductor investment and cooperation from Japanese companies. Rahman further referred to the Chief Minister's Japan visit after polling in Assam and before the counting of votes, questioning the circumstances surrounding the visit.

data.title: GAIL Looks to Sell Its Stake in US Shale Biz
data.description:
Kalpana Pathak Mumbai: GAIL (India)'s US unit is close to selling its entire 20% stake in oil and gas assets at Eagle Ford shale basin in Texas, said executives aware of the development. The state-run gas distributor has received a few expressions of interest from US-based companies and is reviewing them, the executives said. "GAIL is evaluating the few expressions of interest it has received and plans to complete the sale process by next month," one of the executives said, adding the company could garner about 100 crore from the deal, which it intends to complete this month.

GAIL didn't respond to an email query. The Eagle Ford shale basin had been witnessing declining output for the past few years. GAIL Global (USA) (GGUI), its wholly owned unit, had floated a tender last February to sell its entire 20% non-operated working interest in oil and gas assets in the Eagle Ford shale basin.

The assets comprise interests in 91 oil and gas wells and 13 identified proved undeveloped locations, covering 2,870 net acres in La Salle and Frio counties. GAIL entered the US shale gas sector in September 2011, taking a 20% interest in Carrizo Oil & Gas' Eagle Ford acreage for $95 million.

The investment comprised an upfront cash payment of $63.7 million and a $31.3 million carry linked to future drilling and development costs. The proposed exit follows similar moves by other Indian energy companies like RIL, which sold its remaining Eagle Ford shale assets in 2021, exiting its decade-long US shale gas business. RIL had earlier offloaded its stake in the Marcellus shale blocks.

data.title: Takeda and DRL to Sell Dengue Prevention Vax
data.description: Our Bureau Mumbai: Japanese pharma giant Takeda and Hyderabad-based Dr. Reddy's Labs (DRL) have paired up to promote and distribute Qdenga, a pioneering vaccine used to prevent dengue. Expected to be launched in the first half of 2027, it will be targeted at the private market for paediatric and adult vaccination for those between four and 60 years of age. The $28 billion Takeda said it will lend its global expertise in vaccines research to the extensive healthcare network and commercial reach of Dr. Reddy's Labs in India. The expected price range for Qdenga was not disclosed. Prices for Qdenga varies widely and hinges on the paying power. In a few European countries, Qdenga is priced at over $200 for two doses while in markets like Indonesia, the vaccine is priced at $80 for the full course. India's top regulatory agency, the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) approved the vaccine for use in July 2026.

data.title: A Clean Sweep by Dishwashers, Powered by GST
data.description:
Writankar Mukherjee Kolkata: The dishwasher is finally finding its rightful place in Indian kitchens, thanks to a drop in prices after goods and services tax (GST) cuts last year, helping turn the premium lifestyle appliance into one of the fastest-growing mainstream categories in the consumer durable market. The pace of sales growth has more than tripled since the tax rationalisation, said manufacturers and retailers.

Notably, Tier II cities have emerged as a new growth engine accounting for nearly 30% of total unit sales, marking a shift for a product that until recently saw demand solely from major cities. Dishwasher sales surged 49% year-on-year (yoy) in the first six months of 2026. Sales of higher-capacity models, having 15 place settings, surged 137% during the period, showed data from sales tracker NielsenIQ, shared by manufacturers.

The government lowered GST on dishwashers by 10 percentage points to 18% with effect from September 22, 2025. Manufacturers dropped prices by 4,500-7,500, now starting at around 25,000, bringing it almost on par with a fridge or a washing machine. Tax cut advertisements by the government also brought the dishwasher category into mainstream attention, boosting demand, according to industry executives. "While the GST rate cut had a favourable impact last year, we have also gone a step ahead to create the category by demystifying the myths," said Saif Khan, managing director at BSH Home Appliances India, which sells Bosch and Siemens brand of dishwashers. "In fact, our 30-day return period had less than 0.1% return of the appliance." The efforts are bearing fruit as BSH surpassed its entire calendar 2025 sales of more than 114,000 dishwashers this August, said Khan.

The turnaround in sales of dishwashers, considered a premium and aspirational product, comes after a brief Covid-era boost, followed by a sales decline during calendar 2022 and 2023. Manufacturers said the resurgence in consumer interest after the GST reduction has given them room to aggressively build the category, from adapting machines for Indian utensils and cooking styles to offering 30-day trials.

From features like 'kadai wash', ability to clean masala stains, biryani pots and pressure cookers, companies have heavily customised the machines originally designed only for Western-style dishes. Sanjay Chitkara, co-chief sales and marketing officer at LG Electronics India, said the GST reduction had made dishwashers more affordable while changing consumer perception of the product from a lifestyle purchase to a useful household appliance. "Today, LG is present primarily in the premium and mid segments of dishwashers, but we are working to make dishwashers accessible to a much wider consumer base," he said.

Despite the rapid growth, dishwashers still remain a small category, with penetration at around 0.5% of Indian households. The market is now about half the size of the microwave oven market estimated at about 2,000 crore. In contrast, dishwasher penetration in the US and Western Europe is at 70-75%. "Few years ago, dishwashers were still an exotic product," said Shibashish Roy, chief executive at Infiniti Retail, which operates Croma stores. "Dishwashers have seen 60% volume growth yoy.

This growth is a result of urbanisation, rising participation of women in the workforce, higher incomes and the GST boost." The current low penetration and high demand has prompted companies like Haier to enter the segment. IFB Industries' FY26 balance sheet also showed a 28% increase in stock-in-trade of dishwashers. Croma is now pushing appliances such as dishwashers as part of its effort to offset weaker mobile-phone sales, where prices have risen sharply this year.

data.title: Price on IEX Soars on High Power Demand
data.description: Shilpa Samant New Delhi: The High Price Day-Ahead Market (HP-DAM) on the Indian Energy Exchange has rallied, often touching the maximum ceiling of 20 per unit through much of September, as sustained electricity demand, particularly during non-solar hours, has increased pressure supply. IEX data for September 6-17 shows the HP-DAM daily market clearing price reaching the 20 per unit ceiling during the period, with most trade in time blocks of non-solar hours, alongside a sharp rise in purchase bids.

data.title: Cover Drive: More Indians Basking in Sun(screen)
data.description:
Aanya Thakur Mumbai: India's increasingly scorching weather is helping sunscreen find a place in the sun, with the number of households buying it more than tripling in four years to 14.3 million as of June 2026, according to a Worldpanel by Numerator report shared exclusively with ET.

This indicates compound annual growth rate of 36% from 4.2 million households in June 2022, pushing the once-niche beauty category into the mainstream, driven by greater awareness of sun exposure, hotter and more unpredictable weather, wider availability, more accessible price points and its growing appeal as both daily sun protection and an anti-ageing staple.

Younger consumers are also incorporating sun protection into daily skincare routines, rather than treating it as a seasonal product, said Manoj Menon, director, commercial, South Asia, at Worldpanel by Numerator (formerly Kantar). Growth is also spreading beyond major cities. "While urban India is the principal growth engine, rural growth is significant and indicates that sun care is no longer an exclusively metropolitan category," Menon said. "However, penetration remains relatively low, suggesting substantial headroom for growth in brands can improve engagement and affordability." Rural penetration of sunscreen has tripled in the same period to 2.4% while urban penetration has reached 7.1%, the report said.

The sunscreen market in India stretches from low-priced mass products to specialised premium formulations. Large FMCG companies are focusing on affordability, while beauty brands are pushing sunscreen as part of everyday skincare and offering products for different skin types and concerns. Hindustan Unilever is pushing sunscreen across price points, starting from a Rs 10 SPF 50 Lakme sunscreen, aimed at widening access and increasing penetration.

It sells premium products under Minimalist and Simple brands. "There are 200 million women stepping out to work. As they do that, this country is becoming hotter, so you can imagine the need for a basic sunscreen is very high," said Priya Nair, managing director and CEO of Hindustan Unilever.

data.title: 'Delays can create gaps in meeting critical defence requirements & increase risk of technology obsolescence'
data.description:
defence minister calls for realistic project timelines Rahul Tripathi Bengaluru: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Friday raised concerns over delays in critical defence projects and urged the scientists and engineers at Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) to create "technologies that do not exist today".

Singh was speaking at the handing over of two Light Combat Aircraft (LCA) Tejas Final Operational Clearance (FOC) Twin Seater Trainers and three HTT-40 Basic Trainers to the Indian Air Force (IAF), and four Dhruv Next Generation (NG) helicopters to Pawan Hans Limited (PHL).

Singh called for realistic project timelines to address delays in ongoing technical projects. He noted that delays can create gaps in meeting critical defence requirements, lead to cost escalations and increase the risk of technology obsolescence. Terming R&D a crucial priority area, Singh urged "young scientists, engineers, designers, test pilots, and technicians to take it as a challenge to create technologies that do not exist today." He called upon them to develop capabilities that secure a leading position for India in the global aerospace technology landscape over the coming decade. "There is a need for enhanced public-private synergy to build next-gen indigenous aerospace capabilities.

By working together, we can accelerate the growth of India's aerospace sector. We must prepare for the sector's transformation through Artificial Intelligence, autonomous systems, unmanned aerial systems, electronic warfare, cyber technologies, and next-generation propulsion, with a strong focus on their indigenous development and integration. Let us all resolve to make India not only self-reliant in the field of aerospace technology but also a global leader," he said.

data.title: Fujifilm Eyes India Semiconductor Opportunity, Inks Pact with Tata Elec
data.description:
Dia Rekhi New Delhi: Japan's Fujifilm is exploring technology transfer opportunities with Indian companies in the semiconductor space, specifically quality control capabilities, Tetsuya Iwasaki, executive vice president and general manager, electronic materials business division told ET, while underscoring the potential of semiconductor materials as a key growth driver for the group.

Fujifilm on Thursday said it is investing about 800 crore to establish a semiconductor materials plant in the Dholera Special Investment Region (DSIR) in phases. It also signed a strategic memorandum of understanding with Tata Electronics to accelerate the development of India's semiconductor materials ecosystem around the latter's upcoming fab in Dholera, Gujarat. "Apart from starting our manufacturing processes, we are also looking at providing technology and manufacturing process knowledge to Indian players in the space as a separate business vertical," Iwasaki said in an interview at Semicon. "The purity required for semiconductor manufacturing is very high and with material suppliers, the quality level differs, so we are going to look at providing local Indian chemical manufacturers with the technology and quality control capabilities to ensure stable environments and stringent quality standards that are required by the industry." He added that Teiichi Goto, chief executive at Fujifilm reaffirmed the company's belief in developing its semiconductor business in India at a meeting recently with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Iwasaki said Goto believed that semiconductors will be the driving force of Fujifilm's India growth. "We consider India not just as a market to get some profit to produce materials but want to build up the production and business capabilities here from scratch," he said. "We currently have around 10 employees in India but with this investment, that number could go up to 70 in the next five years."

data.title: India’s dairy consumer is changing — And the industry must evolve beyond volume growth
data.description:
For decades, India’s dairy sector has stood as one of the country’s most compelling development success stories. From a milk-deficient nation, we have emerged as the largest producer of milk in the world. This transformation helped in addressing a priority—ensuring availability of milk and integrating millions of farmers into the value chain.

But as we reflect on this achievement, an important question confronts us: Have we solved only for volume, while leaving value behind?

Because the next phase of India’s dairy journey will not be defined by how much more milk we produce, but by how much value we are able to create across the value chain—most importantly for the farmer.

Scale of challenge

A closer look at the structure of the industry reveals the scale of this challenge. Of the roughly 150 million tonnes of marketable surplus milk in the country, the organised sector—cooperatives and private dairies combined—collects only about 55 million metric tonnes. The remaining 90–95 million tonnes continue to flow through informal and unorganized channels.

In effect, a significant part of India’s dairy economy that operates outside the organized sector, in many cases, creates more value per litre than the organized sector does.

This reality becomes especially relevant in the context of the recent increase in milk procurement prices. Across the industry, there has been visible concern around margin pressures, with many players waiting for raw milk prices to soften.

Farmers struggling to keep pace with rising costs

According to a recent commentary by Kuldeep Sharma, Chief Editor of dairy journal Dairy News 7x7, the nominal income of dairy farmers between FY19 and FY25 has grown at a CAGR of about 11.5 per cent, while real income growth has been closer to 5 per cent. This is lower than the overall real GDP growth during the same period, indicating that dairy farmers have struggled to keep pace with rising input costs and inflation.

If farmer economics do not improve in a sustained manner, the long-term stability of the dairy ecosystem itself is at risk. The viability of the producer is the foundation on which the entire industry rests.

We have consistently maintained the need to double the nominal income of our farmer partners over the next five years. In order to achieve this, a CAGR of approximately 14.5 per cent is required against the historic growth of ~11.5 per cent delivered by the sector. This is only possible by creating and capturing greater value in the products sold.

At the same time, the demand environment for dairy in India remains structurally strong. Over the past five years, consumption has grown at an estimated 4–5% annually, driven by urbanisation, rising incomes, increasing awareness of nutrition, and a shift towards protein-rich diets.

Presenting a paradox

Supply, however, has grown at a slightly slower pace—closer to 3–3.5 per cent. While the gap may appear small, in a system of India’s scale, even a modest divergence sustained over several years can create significant supply-demand imbalances and upward pressure on prices. Climate variability only adds to this complexity.

India today presents a paradox. We are the largest producer of milk in the world, yet we import high-value dairy proteins such as whey protein concentrate and milk protein concentrate, while exporting lower-value commodities like skimmed milk powder.

India has already demonstrated that it can solve for scale. The next challenge is to solve for value. Because unless we get this equation right, we will continue to see a situation where volumes grow, but value remains constrained, limiting the potential of farmers, businesses, and the sector as a whole. The opportunity ahead is immense. But realising it will require a conscious move beyond volume growth—and a collective commitment to capturing the true value of what we produce.

The author is CEO,

data.title: EIL Sees More Pipeline and Storage Opportunities in Gulf
data.description:
amid hormuz risks Our Bureau New Delhi: Engineers India (EIL) sees more business opportunities in the Gulf as Saudi Arabia and the UAE plan to expand pipeline and storage infrastructure to reduce their dependence on the Strait of Hormuz, chairman Atul Gupta said on Friday.

The near-closure of the Strait due to the Iran war, which began more than six months ago, has heightened the need for Gulf oil exporters to develop alternative export routes. The war has also damaged energy infrastructure in the region, some of which is now being restored. "This conflict has definitely opened up more opportunities from the (Gulf) region," Gupta said.

Saudi Arabia and the UAE are planning infrastructure, including pipelines and strategic storage, to protect against future disruptions from a closure of the Strait, he said. The projects are still at the planning stage, with EIL involved in some of them.

Order inflow from the Gulf has been slow at about 510 crore so far this fiscal year but is expected to pick up if the situation normalises, Gupta said. EIL's order book stands at about 17,000 crore, with about 43% share coming from overseas projects. Besides its mainstay hydrocarbon business, EIL is receiving significant orders from the fertiliser, metals, defence, nuclear power and data-centre sectors, Gupta said.

data.title: Volkswagen Slashes 2026 Outlook As Porsche Write-Down, China Weakness Weigh; Stock Down
data.description:
BRUSSELS (dpa-AFX) - Volkswagen AG (VOW.BE, VLKAF.PK,VKW.L,VOW.DE) lowered its outlook for fiscal 2026, citing a goodwill impairment related to Porsche AG, a challenging market environment, particularly in China, and additional restructuring expenses.

VOW.DE closed Friday's regular trading at EUR 76.15 down EUR 6.90 or 8.31%.

The automaker now expects group sales revenue of around 315 billion euros in 2026, roughly in line with the midpoint of its previous forecast range of a 3% decline to flat growth from 2025 revenue of 321.9 billion euros.

Volkswagen also reduced its operating return on sales forecast to up to 1%, down from its earlier guidance of 4.0% to 5.5%. The company reported an operating return on sales of 2.8% in 2025.

The revised outlook reflects special items totaling about 10 billion euros that are expected to weigh on operating profit during 2026, including 0.9 billion euros already recorded in the first half of the year. Excluding these special effects, Volkswagen said its operating return on sales would be about 4% for the year.

Volkswagen said operating earnings are being pressured by a further deterioration in market conditions, especially in China, and a faster-than-expected shift in consumer demand toward battery-electric vehicles. The company expects these trends to weigh particularly on the Audi and Volkswagen Passenger Cars brands.

A major factor behind the forecast revision is a non-cash impairment of approximately 6 billion euros related to goodwill allocated to the Porsche business segment. The charge follows updated long-term planning by Porsche AG and revised assumptions used by Volkswagen in assessing the unit's enterprise value. The impairment is expected to reduce the group's operating profit in the third quarter.

In addition, Volkswagen anticipates further restructuring costs tied to expanded early-retirement programs and the planned sale of Volkswagen Osnabrück GmbH under the 'Future of Volkswagen' agreement reached in late 2024. The company also expects non-cash asset impairments at fully consolidated operations in China due to developments in the local automotive market.

Combined, these restructuring and China-related effects are expected to reduce earnings by around €2 billion in the second half of 2026. Volkswagen said most of the additional special items will be recognized in the third quarter.

The company's management and supervisory boards will decide on a dividend proposal for fiscal 2026 at the beginning of 2027, with the payout scheduled for approval at the Annual General Meeting in June 2027.

Volkswagen plans to publish its interim financial statements for the period ended September 30, 2026, on October 29, 2026.

data.title: NASA Just Gave SpaceX Another $946 Million Boost, Adding 3 More Crew Dragon Missions to the ISS Through 2030
data.description:
NASA extended its commercial crew contract with Space Exploration Technologies Corp (NASDAQ:SPCX), adding three crewed Dragon flights to the International Space Station through 2030, worth up to $946 million upon completion.

Deal Deepens NASA’s Reliance on Dual Commercial Partners

The extension brings SpaceX’s total under the Commercial Crew Transportation Capability contract to 17 operational missions. NASA said on Friday that the move helps it “maintain access to the space station with two unique commercial crew industry partners.” Under the full contract, SpaceX will have earned $5.92 billion from NASA.

Boeing Co. (NYSE:BA) is the other partner under NASA’s Commercial Crew Program, providing astronaut transport via its Starliner capsule. NASA and Boeing are targeting an uncrewed cargo flight, Starliner-1, no earlier than the fourth quarter of 2026, according to Boeing’s second-quarter 2026 financial filing.

Modification Covers Full Mission Support Package

SpaceX will handle ground, launch, in-orbit, and return and recovery operations under the modification. The award also covers cargo transportation for each mission and lifeboat capability while Dragon is docked to the space station, according to NASA.

Government contracts from NASA and the Department of Defense continue to support SpaceX’s launch revenue. The company, which went public in June, is reportedly winding down its six-year-old Dragon program as it shifts its focus to Starship, which is still under development, for future missions.

Trading Metrics

SpaceX has a market capitalization of $2.07 trillion, a 52-week high of $225.64 and a 52-week low of $104.83.

The large-cap space stock has gained 6.54% over the past month.

Jewellers face higher hallmarking costs as festive, wedding demand picks up
data.description:
New Delhi, Sept. 19 -- Bengaluru,

Mumbai :

India's jewellers are facing higher compliance costs in the run-up to the festive and wedding season after the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) raised the gold hallmarking fee by 67% to Rs.75 per article from Rs.45 on 14 September.

The increase comes as elevated gold prices have pushed consumers towards lighter jewellery and exchanges, making the flat per-article fee more significant for lower-value pieces and adding to costs for retailers that absorb the charge rather than pass it on to customers.

Amit Modak, chief executive and director of Reva Diamonds by P.N. Gadgil & Sons Ltd, said the additional cost would become meaningful at scale for a retailer that hallmarks a large number of articles.

"The Rs.30 increase per article may appear small in isolation, but when multiplied across the large number of articles that an organized retailer hallmarks, it becomes a meaningful incremental cost," said Modak.

The impact is more pronounced for lightweight jewellery because the same fee applies regardless of weight. Small earrings, rings and pendants have become increasingly relevant as consumers adjust to higher gold prices.

"A lower fee slab for articles below a certain weight could help address the disproportionate impact on small earrings, rings and pendants," Modak said, adding that the BIS, industry, and other stakeholders should decide the threshold through consultation.

Supriya Kataria, founder of Mumbai-based Kumari Fine Jewellery, said her company would charge customers the notified fee at actuals, without adding a margin.

"Hallmarking is a statutory consumer protection fee that directly assures purity and HUID traceability," Kataria said, adding that the company's bulk consignments help optimize the effective per-piece cost.

Darshan Chauhan, chief growth officer and executive director of Sky Gold & Diamonds, also expects limited impact. The company said the revised fee follows its existing billing mechanism through retail partners and would not materially change its operating cost structure. Even for jewellery priced at around Rs.5,000-10,000, the additional Rs.30 represents a small proportion of the purchase value, Chauhan said.

The increase has nevertheless raised concerns among industry representatives about how the charge is collected and its effect on the customer experience.

"The amount is not very big. But the customer refuses it. The customer argues, 'I have taken such a big order. Why are you talking about Rs.35 or Rs.40?'" said Rajesh Rokde, an industry representative at the All India Gem and Jewellery Domestic Council.

Rokde said jewellers face the difficulty of explaining the charge to customers, even though the statutory fee is small compared with the value of a jewellery purchase.

"The customer is already unable to buy because gold is expensive. Secondly, making charges are added to it. Thirdly, GST (goods and services tax) is added to it. Fourthly, hallmark charges have been added to it," he said.

He also said the industry had not been adequately consulted on the increase and called for a review of the fee. "As a government body, they should meet all the associations. Because, after all, only the jeweller will do the collection." The earlier Rs.45 fee was already high, and a lower rate could be considered, he added.

High gold prices- Rs.1,57,860 per 10 grams of 24-carat gold on Friday, up nearly 17% since 1 January-are already pushing consumers towards lighter-weight, lower-carat and studded jewellery, while exchanges have emerged as an important source of demand.

In a 30 July report, the World Gold Council said jewellery demand weakened from mid-May to mid-June as "the month-long inauspicious period (mid-May to mid-June), the 9% import duty hike, and the Prime Minister's appeal to curb gold purchases weighed on demand."

Jewellery demand fell 15% year-on-year to 75 tonnes in the June quarter, although it recovered 14% sequentially from a weak first quarter.

"Volume of the gold jewellery retail sector (in India) will decline 13-15% on year to 620-640 tonnes this fiscal, a level not seen in the past decade," said Himank Sharma, director, credit rating agency Crisil, in a 22 May report.

Amid this shift, a Rs.75 charge represents a larger proportion of the value of a small earring or pendant than a heavier piece, even though both attract the same statutory fee.

According to the BIS's latest notification, gold hallmarking is compulsory in 392 districts, and is being implemented in phases in the 800+ districts.

Mint's queries emailed to the BIS remained unanswered.

Rokde also raised concerns about uneven coverage of mandatory hallmarking across districts, saying differences in implementation could create confusion for customers.

He also raised concerns about fake hallmarking, arguing that higher compliance costs could increase the incentive for malpractice.

More stakeholders are awaiting clarity on rules. "We are waiting for clarity on the new rules as we have seen some jewellers are unhappy with the higher charges," said a Mumbai-based hallmarking laboratory on the condition of anonymity.

Assaying and Hallmarking Centres (AHCs) are independent, third-party laboratories recognized by the BIS to scientifically test the purity of precious metals and apply hallmarks.

He said the number of AHCs is not evenly distributed across the country and is instead concentrated in major cities, reducing accessibility for small regional jewellers. data.title: China investigates Meituan unit for suspected violations of unfair competition laws
data.description:

  • Listed Tongcheng says operating normally

China's market regulator is investigating Meituan unit Beijing Sankuai Information Technology for suspected violations of unfair competition laws, the country's official CCTV broadcaster reported on Saturday.

China has been cracking down on monopolistic behaviour, most recently fining Trip.com $770 million over what the regulator said was its online hotel-booking monopoly, as Beijing struggles to bolster consumption amid a slowing economy.

The Beijing branch of the State Administration for Market Regulation said Hangzhou Taomei Aviation Services, Tongcheng Network Technology and Tujia Online Information Technology (Tianjin) were also subject to investigation after preliminary findings, according to CCTV.

Tongcheng said in a post on its official WeChat account that its operations were normal and that it was cooperating with authorities.

The four companies have not responded to requests for comment from Reuters.

data.title: Perfume makers feel ethanol squeeze, weigh price hikes
data.description:
Bengaluru, Sept. 19 -- Smelling good could get costlier this festive season. Perfume makers are grappling with higher costs of ethanol, a key ingredient in alcohol-based fragrances, and glass bottles, putting pressure on margins and prompting some companies to consider price increases.

Ethanol prices have climbed as tighter domestic supplies and stronger demand from the fuel-blending programme squeeze availability, while glass bottle costs have risen by as much as 20% over the past year, industry executives said.

Vini Cosmetics Pvt. Ltd, which owns the Fogg and Ossum brands, is weighing a price increase during or after the festive season, with a decision expected by October and a possible hike from November. The company, though, has no plans to reduce pack sizes or alter formulations to protect margins.

"It's going to become costlier. That's the only thing I am seeing as of now," said Darshan Patel, founder of Vini Cosmetics. He said that alcohol is currently available, but prices are fluctuating, which is why "we are not in a hurry to increase our price". Glass bottle costs have also risen by almost 20% from a year ago, he added.

Contract manufacturers are facing an even tighter squeeze on ethanol supplies. Subhash Mhatre, partner at Suhan Aerosol, which makes aerosol and fragrance products for Godrej Consumer Products Ltd's Park Avenue, Vanesa Care Pvt. Ltd, VLCC Personal Care Ltd, Wipro Enterprises (P) Ltd and others, said the price of industrial ethanol has risen by 15-20% from a year earlier.

The sharpest increase came between February and April 2026, with ethanol prices continuing to rise in May, when they surged by as much as 50%, he said.

Ethanol accounts for roughly 45% of an alcohol-based perfume formulation, making it one of the biggest input costs, Mhatre said, adding that Suhan Aerosol requires about 60 tonnes of ethanol a month, and securing regular supplies has become considerably more difficult. Even a 20-25-tonne batch now takes an average of 8 to 10 days to arrive.

"Any further increase of 10-20% in ethanol prices would place considerable pressure on the manufacturing economics and margins," he cautioned.

India's perfume market grew from Rs.7,000-8,000 crore in 2019-20 to Rs.12,000-14,000 crore in 2024-25 and is projected to swell to Rs.23,000-28,000 crore by 2029-30, implying a 14-15% annual growth, according to business management consultant Wazir Advisors. Mid- and mass-market perfumes priced below Rs.4,000 account for about 75-85% of the market.

Perfume makers are facing margin pressure as ethanol prices rise amid higher demand from the fuel-blending programme.

Perfume makers require high-purity alcohol, mainly ethanol. Depending on the formulation, they may use highly purified extra-neutral alcohol or denatured alcohol, which contains additives that make it unsuitable for drinking. Alcohol can account for more than half of a perfume product.

An Eau de Toilette typically contains 5-15% fragrance concentrate, while an Eau de Parfum contains 10-20%, according to the Geneva-based International Fragrance Association. The rest is mainly alcohol and water, which carry the fragrance. As more ethanol is diverted for blending with petrol, less is available for non-fuel industries such as perfumes, potentially tightening supplies and pushing up prices.

Ethanol blending in petrol rose to 20% in the 2025-26, up from 12.1% in 2022-23. Procurement of ethanol by India's oil-marketing companies rose to more than 12 billion litres in 2025-26, while production capacity expanded to about 20 billion litres, according to the ministry of petroleum and natural gas.

But most brands are unwilling to raise consumer prices at this stage, Mhatre said. A few domestic brands have agreed to partially offset the higher costs through case-by-case price revisions, while manufacturers continue to absorb a substantial share of the increase, resulting in an estimated 10% hit to profitability.

"The immediate challenge is, therefore, likely to remain margin pressure on manufacturers, rather than visible price hikes for consumers," Mhatre said. He expects ethanol availability to gradually stabilize over the next 6-10 months as production improves, although he does not necessarily expect a meaningful decline in prices.

Vanesa Care, which owns the Denver and Envy brands, has passed on some of the higher costs to consumers, said Saurabh Gupta, director of marketing and sales. The company is locking in alcohol supplies ahead of the festive period.

For Plum, the impact has been delayed because the company is still using cheaper ethanol inventory bought earlier. "So far, we have not seen anything, but I think once the inventory starts running out, we'll start seeing," said founder Shankar Prasad.

Ethanol-linked formulations account for 5-7% of Plum's formulations. But Prasad said cosmetic alcohol comes from specific sources, leaving companies with little flexibility to switch suppliers.

"We are a price taker, so you really can't do anything," Prasad said. "It has to be either absorbed, depending on what the quantum is, or passed on."

Plum has raised prices by roughly 7-10% amid higher packaging and imported raw-material costs. The festive season accounts for about 30% of its annual sales.

Not all fragrance brands are facing the same cost pressures due to the rising ethanol prices. Secret Alchemist co-founder Akash Valia said the brand primarily uses grain-based ethanol and has so far seen little direct impact on costs.

Mass-market perfumes priced about Rs.600-700 typically use more ethanol made from petrochemical feedstocks rather than agricultural sources and could therefore face greater cost pressure, Valia said.

Secret Alchemist raised prices in June amid higher oil-related costs following the escalation of the West Asia conflict. Its glass bottle costs have risen about 15%, while some sensitive fragrance ingredients have become 7-10% more expensive on an industry-wide level.

"The pressure on non-fuel [ethanol] users is more from supply-chain constraints. While they can source ethanol domestically, imports are also used for other applications, and longer transit times and higher shipping costs are creating delays. Ahead of the festive season, players therefore have to look for whatever supply is available domestically," said Poonam Upadhyay, director, Crisil Ratings. data.title: South Korea justice nominee withdraws in Lee's second cabinet setback as polls slide
data.description:
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung's nominee for justice minister withdrew from consideration on Saturday, the second of Lee's cabinet picks to step aside this month as his approval ratings slump.

Kim Seung-won's exit follows the withdrawal of Yong Hye-in as nominee for gender-equality minister on Sunday, in the latest fallout from Lee's cabinet reshuffle in late August.

Kim, who said he did not want to add any burden to Lee's administration, criticised a conservative lawmaker who had accused him of lobbying regulators over a drug trial and of financial irregularities. Kim has denied the allegations.

"I gravely accept that I did not meet the public's expectations, and I will deeply reflect on my shortcomings," Kim told a press conference.

A Gallup Korea poll released on Friday put Lee's public approval at 37%, the lowest since he took office in June 2025, a decline pollsters have partly linked to criticism over his personnel appointments.

At a press conference on Friday, Lee acknowledged shortcomings in his administration's screening of nominees. "We are currently working to reexamine our personnel system," the president said.

data.title: Vietnam to gauge investor interest in sovereign bonds, government says
data.description:
Vietnam's government is preparing to host foreign investors to gauge interest in its bonds, the finance ministry said.

The planned road show is a regular annual event and is not meant to involve an immediate issuance of bonds, the ministry said in a statement issued late on Friday night. It did not say when the event would take place.

"The event provides an opportunity for the debt management authority to gather market feedback and assess investors' level of interest in Vietnamese government bonds," the ministry said.

Reuters reported earlier this week that the ministry was weighing the possible issuance of offshore dollar-denominated bonds after meetings with investment banks.

However, it had not reached a final decision on whether to go ahead with the sale, as it was evaluating the costs of borrowing at a time of rising global yields.

Vietnam's last dollar bond was issued in 2014.

"This is an annual investor engagement program and does not involve an immediate offering or issuance of bonds," the ministry said.

It added that "specific details, such as the size, tenor, or timing of any issuance, will be considered and decided by the government at an appropriate time."

The ministry also said it plans to meet international credit rating agencies as Vietnam pursues an investment-grade sovereign credit rating by the end of the decade.

data.title: Indigenous, civil-society groups sue Prabowo over forest fire response
data.description:
A group of indigenous and civil-society organisations in Indonesia's West Kalimantan has filed a class-action lawsuit against President Prabowo Subianto and other authorities over their handling of forest fires in the region, its lawyer said on Saturday.

Below are more details:

  • The case was registered at the Pontianak court in West Kalimantan with the first hearing scheduled for October 7, the court filing shows.

  • "This lawsuit was filed in response to the West Kalimantan public's concerns over the government's negligence and failure to prevent and tackle forest and land fires that recur every year," Glorio Sanen, the plaintiffs' lawyer told Reuters on Saturday.

  • The presidential office did not immediately respond to request for comment.

  • The plaintiffs are West Kalimantan chapter of the Indigenous Peoples Alliance of the Archipelago, West Kalimantan branch of Catholic Youth, Perkumpulan Laman Punyung Indonesia and an individual, Sisilius Rami, the filing shows.

  • Indonesia is battling its most intense wildfires in 11 years and the government has warned that the fires could continue until November this year.

  • In 2016, a lawsuit was brought by seven Indonesian residents against then-President Joko Widodo, his cabinet ministers and local governments over their handling of forest fires in 2015.

  • After initially winning at the district court, the decision on 2016's lawsuit was overturned when the Supreme Court granted the government's petition for judicial review in 2022, according to media reports.

data.title: Karnataka Approves Sustainable Data Centre Policy, Targets 1 GW IT Load By 2031
data.description:
Karnataka’s new five-year framework links data centre incentives to sustainability while targeting 1 GW of IT load and a 10-12 per cent share of India’s AI-ready capacity by 2031

Karnataka has approved a five-year Sustainable Data Centre Policy for 2026-31, targeting 1 GW of cumulative data centre IT load by 2031 as the state seeks to capture 10-12 per cent of India's AI-ready data centre capacity.

The policy, backed by a revised budget framework of Rs 1,300.45 crore, places sustainability at the centre of Karnataka's next phase of data centre expansion, with incentives linked to power and water efficiency, renewable energy use and other environmental metrics.

The move comes as AI and high-performance computing drive a sharp increase in demand for data centre capacity across India. The country's installed data centre capacity has risen from about 375 MW in 2020 to around 1,575 MW currently, according to the central government.

Karnataka's new policy covers investments across data centre units, parks and operators, as well as edge data centres, cable landing stations and allied infrastructure. It also seeks to spread capacity beyond Bengaluru through regional digital corridors.

"Karnataka was among the early states to recognise the importance of data centres and create a policy framework to support their growth. But the technology landscape has changed significantly, particularly with the rapid growth of AI, and we have also become more conscious of the environmental footprint of this infrastructure," Karnataka IT-BT and E-Governance Minister Priyank Kharge said.

The policy provides for renewable energy adoption, advanced cooling systems, water management and monitoring of power usage effectiveness (PUE) and water usage effectiveness (WUE). It also envisages performance-linked incentives to encourage more efficient use of electricity and water.

Weighing in on the new state policy, Piyush Somani, Promoter, Managing Director and Chairman at ESDS Software Solution, said it could help create a stronger environment for long-term data centre investments as AI and other high-compute technologies increase demand for computing infrastructure.

"The ambition to reach 1 GW of data centre IT load by 2031, while positioning Karnataka to account for 10-12 per cent of India's AI-ready capacity, reflects the scale of computing infrastructure that emerging technologies will require," Somani said.

He said that the policy's focus on investment incentives, ease of doing business and support for AI and other high-compute technologies could support the expansion of the sector.

Somani also pointed out the policy's emphasis on developing data centre infrastructure beyond Bengaluru as an opportunity to create a more distributed digital infrastructure base across Karnataka.

Karnataka had been working on a sustainability-focused data centre framework amid concerns over the sector's power and water consumption. In March, Kharge said the government was reviewing its earlier data centre policy and was considering locations such as Mangaluru, where subsea cable connectivity could support future facilities.

The state had earlier outlined plans for sustainable data centre parks across Bengaluru, Mysuru and Mangaluru with a combined capacity of 1 GW, including a proposed 500 MW park near Hoskote.

The new policy also proposes data centre resource heat mapping to assess the availability of water and energy when selecting sites. It envisages dedicated Sustainable Data Centre Zones and Data Centre Parks, alongside a Centre of Excellence focused on applied research, innovation and ecosystem development.

Karnataka will offer incentives covering capital investment, project establishment, land, connectivity, electricity, green energy, access to demand centres, research and development, skilling and participation by micro, small and medium enterprises.

The policy also provides for AI- and quantum-ready facilities, intelligent data centres, edge computing and cable landing infrastructure.

"Our objective is not simply to add more capacity, but to build the right capacity, in the right locations and with the right infrastructure," Kharge said, adding that the state would focus on renewable energy, newer cooling technologies, water management and stronger connectivity.

Implementation will be anchored by the Department of Electronics, Information Technology, Biotechnology and Science & Technology, with Karnataka Information Technology Services (KITS) serving as the registration and policy interface. Karnataka Udyoga Mitra will act as the single-window agency for clearances.

The policy marks a shift from Karnataka's earlier 2022-27 data centre framework, which sought to attract around Rs 10,000 crore in investment and develop more than 200 MW of capacity by 2025, while also encouraging renewable-powered and energy-efficient facilities.

data.title: Rakesh Kumar Singh Elevated To CEO At Capacit'e Infraprojects
data.description:
Brings extensive experience in construction, project management, operations, quality, safety and regional business leadership

Rakesh Kumar Singh has been elevated to Chief Executive Officer at Capacit'e Infraprojects, marking a new leadership role after an extensive career across construction, infrastructure and project management. Singh has previously held senior positions at Capacit'e Infraprojects and other major engineering and construction organisations.

Experience At Capacit'e

Before his elevation, Singh served as President and Regional Head – North at Capacit'e Infraprojects. His experience at the organisation has included regional leadership and operational responsibilities across the construction business.

His elevation follows a career spanning project execution, operations, construction management and business leadership across the infrastructure sector.

Leadership Across Construction

Prior to joining Capacit'e Infraprojects, Singh held senior operational roles at B L Kashyap & Sons, including Senior Vice President Operations and Regional Head, as well as Vice President Operations.

He also served as Head of Operations at Shapoorji Pallonji Group, adding experience in managing construction and operational functions.

Diverse Project Experience

Singh's earlier career includes roles at JMC Projects (India), where he served as Assistant Vice President – Operations and Senior General Manager. He was also Deputy General Manager at Tata Projects and General Manager at CBRE.

Earlier assignments included Project Manager and Assistant Construction Manager roles at L&T Construction, followed by an engineering position at Consulting Engineering Services.

Focus On Operations

Across these roles, Singh has worked across project management, construction, operations, quality and safety. His career has covered different stages of project execution and regional operations within the construction and infrastructure sectors.

As CEO, Singh will take on broader leadership responsibilities at Capacit'e Infraprojects, building on his previous experience with the organisation and his wider background in construction and project operations.

data.title: Enablence Technologies Inc. Closes C$25 Million Strategic Investment
data.description:
Ottawa, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - September 18, 2026) - Enablence Technologies Inc. ("Enablence" or the "Company"), a leading provider of planar lightwave circuit (PLC) optical chips for datacom, telecom, artificial intelligence (AI), and advanced vision applications, is pleased to announce that further to its news release dated September 15, 2026, it has closed its private placement with Collingwood Investments Incorporated (the "Investor") of 3,226,000 common shares of the Company (the "Common Shares") at a price of C$7.75 per Common Share for gross proceeds to the Company of approximately C$25 million (the "Offering").

The Company intends to use the net proceeds of the Offering for planned capital expenditures to expand capacity at its fab facilities in Silicon Valley and Vietnam, working capital to support growing sales volumes, and general corporate purposes.

Concurrent with the closing of the Offering, the Company entered into an investor rights agreement with the Investor (the "Investor Rights Agreement") which provides, among other things, pro rata pre-emptive rights on all future issuances of equity securities by the Company and certain top-up rights in favour of the Investor. A copy of the Investor Rights Agreement will be available in due course on SEDAR+ (www.sedarplus.ca) under the Company's issuer profile.

The Common Shares issued pursuant to the Offering are subject to a statutory hold period of four months and one day from the closing date in accordance with applicable Canadian securities laws. The Offering remains subject to final acceptance of the TSX Venture Exchange.

Paradigm Capital Inc. acted as exclusive financial advisor to the Company in connection with the Offering and is entitled to an advisory cash fee equal to 5% of the gross proceeds of the Offering. Bennett Jones LLP acted as legal advisor to the Company in connection with the Offering.

About Enablence Technologies Inc.

Enablence is a publicly traded company listed on the TSX Venture Exchange that designs, markets and sells optical chips and sub systems, primarily in the form of planar lightwave circuits (PLC), on silicon-based chips for datacom, telecom, automotive and artificial intelligence (AI) applications. Enablence products serve a global customer base, primarily focused today on data center and other rapidly growing end markets. Enablence also works with customers that have emerging market uses for its technology, including medical devices, automotive LiDAR, and virtual and augmented reality headsets. In select strategic circumstances, the Company also uses its proprietary, non-captive fabrication plant in Fremont, California to manufacture chips designed by third party customers.
